body.message: A standard discounted cash flow valuation isn't suitable for Rivian Automotive, Inc. No intrinsic value is reported, deliberately: the model would produce a figure with no economic meaning.
reasons:
The company is loss-making: its day-to-day business lost $3.6bn in its 2025 financial year, and it made a loss in 4 of the last 4 years.
    This kind of valuation assumes a business that already makes a profit and grows steadily. Applying it to a loss-making company would mean inventing the profits it then puts a value on.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.detail: 3-year revenue CAGR, FY2022-FY2025 (1.7bn -> 5.4bn); raw 48.1% clamped to [0%, 25%]

assumptions.name: operating_margin
assumptions.detail: the latest year's -66.5%; the margin has moved one way for 4 years (improving) rather than spiking, so the level reached is used

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.detail: normalized effective rate as published, median over 3 year(s), because no profitable year in the window

assumptions.name: da_pct
assumptions.detail: median D&A / revenue over 3 years

assumptions.name: capex_terminal_pct
assumptions.detail: mean capex / revenue over 3 years

assumptions.name: capex_pct
assumptions.detail: capex / revenue, trailing twelve months; fades from 24.1% (current) to 25.9% (3-yr mean) over the forecast

assumptions.name: nwc_pct
assumptions.detail: median working capital as a share of revenue across FY2022-FY2025 (4 years)

assumptions.name: wacc
assumptions.detail: CAPM: 4.18% + 1.45x4.41% = 10.58% equity; debt 6.84% (5.09% after tax); weights 76.8%E / 23.2%D

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.detail: held at long-run US nominal growth (Fed SEP, Sep 2026: 2.0% real GDP + 2.0% PCE inflation) rather than at the 4.18% risk-free rate, because no company outgrows its own economy in perpetuity; adjustable downward to 0%

assumptions.name: projection_years
assumptions.detail: ten years rather than five, because 25.0% growth needs room to slow to the 4.0% it ends at

assumptions.name: fade_enabled
assumptions.detail: on; growth glides from 25.0% down to 4.0% across the forecast rather than dropping to it in one step at the end

assumptions.name: fade_start_year
assumptions.detail: the glide starts immediately, so 25.0% is this year's rate rather than the next three years' rate

body.disclaimer: Rivian Automotive, Inc. loses money, so a standard valuation was refused: it has no profits to project. This figure is not a valuation and must not be treated as one. It was produced only because it was explicitly requested, and it rests entirely on assumptions about a future that has not happened: that revenue grows 8.4% a year, that the operating margin climbs from -67% to 10% within 6 years, that the company can fund about $12.9bn of losses along the way, and that it then performs like an established, profitable business indefinitely. Loss-making companies often never reach sustained profitability; many raise money on terms that dilute existing shareholders, and some fail outright, in which case shareholders can lose everything. Modest changes to these assumptions move this figure by multiples, not percentages - the sensitivity table shows how far. It is not investment advice, a price target, or a reason to buy or sell.
why_standard_valuation_refused:
The company is loss-making: its day-to-day business lost $3.6bn in its 2025 financial year, and it made a loss in 4 of the last 4 years.
    This kind of valuation assumes a business that already makes a profit and grows steadily. Applying it to a loss-making company would mean inventing the profits it then puts a value on.

assumptions.name: speculative_revenue_growth
assumptions.detail: the lower of the latest year's revenue growth (8.4%) and the 3-year CAGR (48.1%), so an early ramp from a small base is not extrapolated

assumptions.name: target_operating_margin
assumptions.detail: a generic mature-company operating margin. It is not specific to this company or its industry, and the company has never earned it

assumptions.name: years_to_profitability
assumptions.detail: the distance from today's -67% operating margin to the 10% target, closed at 15 percentage points a year - a fast pace to sustain

assumptions.name: post_profitability_growth
assumptions.detail: half the 8.4% assumed until profitability, as growth slows with scale; floored at terminal growth

assumptions.name: mature_capex_pct
assumptions.detail: investment settles at 20.0% of revenue (moderated down from today's 24.1%), with depreciation rising to 13.5% - 67% of it, which is what Total Market companies cover out of depreciation (Damodaran). The 6.5% gap is the net investment the growth is paid for with.

assumptions.name: mature_da_pct
assumptions.detail: 67% of the 20.0% invested, which is what Total Market companies cover out of depreciation (Damodaran). The 6.5% gap is net investment, and it does not go away

assumptions.name: mature_nwc_pct
assumptions.detail: the company's working-capital investment of -2.6% of revenue growth, limited to [0%, 10%] once mature

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.detail: US statutory rate. A loss-maker's tax history says nothing about a profitable future, and accumulated tax losses that would shelter early profits are not credited, which errs low

assumptions.name: wacc
assumptions.detail: CAPM: 4.18% + 1.45x4.41% = 10.58% equity; debt 6.84% (5.09% after tax); weights 76.8%E / 23.2%D; that gave 9.30%, raised to a 10% floor for a company that has never been profitable

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.detail: conservative long-run default; adjustable

assumptions.name: projection_years
assumptions.detail: years of mature-company forecast after profitability, before the terminal value

wacc_inputs.name: risk_free_rate
wacc_inputs.detail: US Treasury 10-year par yield as of 2025-12-31 (Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates)

wacc_inputs.name: beta
wacc_inputs.detail: Blume-adjusted from raw 1.67; computed from 59 monthly returns vs ^GSPC (5y), the convention market data providers use

wacc_inputs.name: cost_of_debt
wacc_inputs.detail: median interest expense / average debt (FY2025, FY2024, FY2023, FY2022)

warnings: On this path Rivian Automotive, Inc. burns $12.9bn of cash before turning profitable, against $6.2bn of cash and investments today. It would have to raise the difference, most likely by issuing shares that dilute existing holders - if it can raise it at all. The estimate subtracts the cost of those losses but assumes the money is found.

Rivian Automotive, Inc.'s gross margin was 3% in its 2025 financial year, below the 10% operating margin assumed. Reaching it needs gross margin to rise well above today's level before operating costs are even covered.
Even on these assumptions, the losses on the way and the debt outweigh the value of the profitable business at the end, so the estimate is negative.

Rivian Automotive, Inc. currently frees up cash from stock, customer payments and supplier bills as it grows, which a maturing business rarely keeps doing. The estimate assumes this stops once the business matures.
Rivian Automotive, Inc.'s calculated discount rate was 9.3%. For a company that has never made a profit, the estimate uses at least 10%, to reflect the extra risk of it never getting there.

body.message: A standard discounted cash flow valuation isn't suitable for American Express Company. No intrinsic value is reported, deliberately: the model would produce a figure with no economic meaning.
reasons: American Express Company is a Credit Services company with a loan book 3.1 times its annual revenue. Lending is part of how it earns that revenue rather than how it is financed, so - as for a bank - unlevered free cash flow and an enterprise-to-equity bridge are not meaningful, and a DCF would produce a figure with no economic meaning. A dividend discount model is not substituted either: it counts only dividends, and American Express Company returned $5.8bn through buybacks against $2.3bn in dividends in its 2025 financial year, so it would understate what shareholders receive. The appropriate tool is an excess-return model, which values a lender from its return on equity against its cost of equity. That model is not available yet, so no value is reported.

assumptions.detail: 3-year revenue CAGR, FY2022-FY2025 (52.9bn -> 72.2bn)

assumptions.name: operating_margin
assumptions.detail: the latest year's 30.5%, which sits inside the previous years' own range (23.4% to 32.1%)

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.detail: median effective rate over 3 profitable year(s)

assumptions.name: da_pct
assumptions.detail: median D&A / revenue over 3 years

assumptions.name: capex_terminal_pct
assumptions.detail: mean capex / revenue over 3 years

assumptions.name: capex_pct
assumptions.detail: median capex / revenue over 3 years (no trailing figure reported)

assumptions.name: nwc_pct
assumptions.detail: no balance sheet reported current assets and liabilities; working capital assumed to stay flat

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.detail: held at long-run US nominal growth (Fed SEP, Sep 2026: 2.0% real GDP + 2.0% PCE inflation) rather than at the 4.18% risk-free rate, because no company outgrows its own economy in perpetuity; adjustable downward to 0%
